items.description: Analyze repository structure and tooling capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a document (results/repo_analysis.md) listing all modules (.archivara/, .opencode/, agent definitions), their purposes, available tools (semantic_scholar, concept_evolve), and the empty scaffolds (figures/, results/) that will be populated during research.

items.description: Conduct web-based literature review on N-body gravity simulation methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Use web search and Semantic Scholar to find at least 10 relevant papers covering: (a) classical N-body methods (direct summation, Barnes-Hut tree codes), (b) symplectic and Verlet integrators, (c) fast multipole methods, (d) GPU-accelerated gravity solvers. Summarize findings in results/literature_review.md with full citations.

items.description: Create and maintain sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib exists at repo root with at least 10 valid BibTeX entries covering: Aarseth (N-body methods), Barnes & Hut (1986 tree code), Verlet (1967 integration), Greengard & Rokhlin (FMM), at least 2 modern GPU N-body papers, at least 2 papers on symplectic integrators, and at least 2 open-source gravity simulation codebases (e.g., REBOUND, Gadget).

items.description: Delegate literature-graph mining for cross-domain gravity simulation insights
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a literature-graph-miner subagent to traverse citation graphs starting from Barnes & Hut (1986) and Verlet (1967). Produce results/citation_graph_analysis.md identifying at least 5 high-impact descendant papers and 3 cross-domain connections (e.g., molecular dynamics, astrophysics, game physics).

items.description: Define problem scope and constraints for the minimal gravity simulation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/problem_definition.md specifying: target particle count range (10-10000), dimensionality (2D and/or 3D), integration method requirements, performance targets (real-time for N<=1000), accuracy requirements (energy conservation within 1% over 1000 timesteps), language choice (Python with optional C/Rust extensions), and visualization requirements.

items.description: Explore concept tree for gravity simulation design space
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept_evolve to generate an initial concept tree in results/concept_evolve/tree/ exploring at least 3 branches: (a) integration algorithms, (b) force calculation strategies, (c) spatial data structures. Each branch must have at least 2 leaf nodes with viability scores.

items.description: Implement direct-summation O(N^2) gravity solver as baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/direct.py implementing: (a) Newtonian gravitational force calculation with softening parameter, (b) particle state representation (position, velocity, mass), (c) brute-force O(N^2) pairwise force accumulation. Must pass a unit test verifying two-body Kepler orbit against analytical solution (semi-major axis error < 1%).

items.description: Implement Leapfrog (Stormer-Verlet) time integrator
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/integrators/leapfrog.py implementing the kick-drift-kick leapfrog scheme. Must demonstrate symplectic energy conservation: total energy drift < 0.1% over 10,000 steps for a stable 3-body configuration. Include comparison against forward Euler showing Euler's energy divergence.

items.description: Build metrics and benchmarking framework
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/metrics.py providing: (a) wall-clock timing per simulation step, (b) total energy computation (kinetic + potential), (c) energy conservation error tracking, (d) angular momentum conservation tracking, (e) benchmark runner that sweeps N from 10 to 5000 and records timing. Output results to results/baseline_benchmarks.json.

items.description: Create basic 2D visualization for simulation validation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/visualization.py that renders particle positions as a 2D scatter plot (using matplotlib). Must support: (a) single-frame snapshot saved to figures/, (b) animated GIF output for trajectory visualization, (c) energy plot over time. Produce figures/baseline_two_body.gif showing a stable two-body orbit.

items.description: Delegate subagent exploration of baseline performance bottlenecks
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent to analyze the baseline O(N^2) solver's scaling behavior and identify the top 3 computational bottlenecks. Document findings in results/concept_evolve/tree/bottleneck_analysis/ with specific recommendations for Phase 3 optimizations, referencing prior work from sources.bib.

items.description: Implement Barnes-Hut tree-code O(N log N) gravity solver
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/barnes_hut.py implementing: (a) recursive quadtree (2D) / octree (3D) spatial decomposition, (b) multipole acceptance criterion (theta parameter, default 0.5), (c) center-of-mass approximation for distant nodes. Must produce force accuracy within 1% of direct summation for a random 1000-particle configuration.

items.description: Implement adaptive timestep control
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/integrators/adaptive.py implementing timestep adaptation based on particle acceleration magnitudes (Aarseth criterion). Must demonstrate: (a) at least 2x speedup over fixed-timestep for a collapsing cluster scenario, (b) energy conservation within 0.5% over the simulation, (c) correct handling of close encounters with reduced timestep.

items.description: Explore and implement NumPy-vectorized force computation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/vectorized.py using NumPy broadcasting for O(N^2) force calculation without Python loops. Must achieve at least 10x speedup over pure-Python direct.py for N=1000 particles. Benchmark results appended to results/baseline_benchmarks.json.

items.description: Concept-tree evolution for novel optimization strategies
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept_evolve to explore optimization strategies beyond Barnes-Hut in results/concept_evolve/tree/optimizations/. Must evaluate at least 4 candidate approaches (e.g., particle-mesh, FMM-lite, spatial hashing, SIMD vectorization) with feasibility scores. Prune to top 2 candidates with written justification referencing literature from sources.bib.

items.description: Implement selected novel optimization from concept-tree exploration
items.acceptance_criteria: Based on item_015 results, implement the highest-scored feasible optimization in src/gravity/. Must include: (a) working implementation with tests, (b) documented complexity analysis, (c) benchmark showing improvement over vectorized baseline for N >= 2000.

items.description: Delegate cross-domain reframing of gravity simulation problem
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent to reframe the gravity simulation problem across at least 5 domains (e.g., molecular dynamics, electrostatics, fluid simulation, machine learning force fields, graph neural networks). Document transferable techniques in results/concept_evolve/tree/cross_domain/ with at least 3 actionable insights that could improve the simulation.

items.description: Run scaling experiments across all solver implementations
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute benchmarks for N in {10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000} across all solvers (direct, vectorized, Barnes-Hut, novel optimization). Record wall-clock time, energy error, and angular momentum error. Save structured results to results/scaling_experiments.json and produce figures/scaling_comparison.png showing log-log timing plots with fitted complexity curves.

items.description: Run accuracy experiments comparing integrators
items.acceptance_criteria: Compare Euler, Leapfrog, and adaptive integrators on: (a) two-body Kepler problem (eccentricity 0.5, 100 orbits), (b) Pythagorean three-body problem, (c) random 100-particle cluster. Measure energy drift, phase-space error, and computational cost. Save to results/integrator_comparison.json and produce figures/energy_conservation.png.

items.description: Conduct Barnes-Hut theta parameter sensitivity analysis
items.acceptance_criteria: Sweep theta in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5} for N=1000 particles. Measure force accuracy (RMS error vs. direct summation), timing, and energy conservation. Produce figures/theta_sensitivity.png showing accuracy-speed tradeoff curve. Identify optimal theta value for <1% force error.

items.description: Reproduce a known N-body benchmark from literature
items.acceptance_criteria: Select one benchmark from sources.bib (e.g., Plummer sphere collapse, Hernquist profile relaxation) and reproduce it using the implemented solvers. Compare results quantitatively against published values. Document reproduction in results/benchmark_reproduction.md with figures saved to figures/.

items.description: Delegate experiment analysis synthesis via subagent
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a literature-graph-miner subagent to compare experimental results from items 018-021 against performance claims in cited papers from sources.bib. Produce results/literature_comparison.md identifying where the minimal sim matches, exceeds, or falls short of published results, with at least 5 specific quantitative comparisons.

items.description: Write comprehensive technical report
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/technical_report.md containing: (a) Abstract, (b) Introduction with problem motivation, (c) Related Work section citing at least 8 entries from sources.bib, (d) Methods section describing all implementations, (e) Results with embedded figure references, (f) Discussion comparing against prior work, (g) Conclusion with future work. Minimum 2000 words.

items.description: Generate final concept-tree summary and research map
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/final_summary.md synthesizing all concept-tree explorations from Phases 1-4. Include: (a) complete tree visualization (text-based), (b) which branches were pursued vs. pruned and why, (c) key insights discovered through concept evolution, (d) suggested future branches for continued research.

items.description: Update README.md with project overview and usage instructions
items.acceptance_criteria: README.md contains: (a) project title and one-paragraph description, (b) installation instructions (dependencies, Python version), (c) usage examples showing how to run each solver, (d) summary of key results with links to figures/, (e) references to sources.bib, (f) repository structure diagram.

items.description: Create reproducibility package
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce: (a) requirements.txt listing all Python dependencies with pinned versions, (b) a run_all.py script that executes the complete experiment pipeline (benchmarks, accuracy tests, figure generation), (c) results/reproducibility_checklist.md confirming all figures and results can be regenerated from scratch.

items.description: Delegate final review via subagent for completeness and quality
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent to audit the entire results/ directory and verify: (a) all acceptance criteria from items 001-026 have corresponding artifacts, (b) sources.bib has at least 10 entries and all are referenced in the technical report, (c) all figures are properly generated and referenced, (d) concept tree has at least 3 branches with 2+ leaves each. Produce results/final_audit.md with pass/fail for each item.
